purpose gap: Purpose (nightly dated gzip tar of /etc/puppetlabs with N-day retention) matches the header ('provides puppet backups') and puppet_backup.pp/backup.pp/backup.sh.erb. Tested: the rendered Hiera values and 0755 root script, the 23:00 crontab entry, the backup directory (local change #14), a run producing a gzip archive that restores puppet.conf byte for byte, retention deleting only the prefix's >9-day archive (12-day gone, 5-day and other-prefix 30-day kept), and a failed run's non-zero exit plus ERROR line on stderr and in the journal (local change #15). Uncovered row (cron firing at 23:00) is honest. GAP: outcome 5 claims a failed run 'deletes no old archive', mapped to a-failed-run-is-loud, but that check does not probe it: it only checks puppet.example.com-recent.tar.gz (5 days old, outside the find -mtime +9 retention, so a run reaching the retention loop keeps it too), no >9-day archive of the prefix remains at that point (the earlier run deleted the 12-day one), and the directory is bind-mounted read-only so rm -f could not delete anything anyway. The 'exit before retention' half of change #15 thus holds with or without the exit; the lab CAN exercise it, e.g. plant a >9-day prefix archive and make tar fail while the directory stays writable (a full small tmpfs over the backup directory, or an unreadable/missing target), then check that archive is still there.
